newsitem.title: USA: M&A backlog high at Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: M&A backlog high at Morgan Stanley.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co has a large backlog in mergers & acquisitions (M&A) activity pointing to continued strong performance in that segment in the second half of the fiscal year, chief financial officer Robert Scott said in an interview Wednesday.
"I would say that we have a good backlog and that suggests we should see a reasonably high level of activity in the second half," Scott said. He declined to provide any figures.
In the company's fiscal second-quarter results announced earlier Wednesday, the value of M&A transactions in the quarter totaled $85.6 billion.
M&A announced transactions were $98.5 billion in the fiscal second quarter a year ago, and $31.7 billion in the three months ended February 28, 1997.

Scott said Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co is already starting to see benefits from its own merger which joined the Morgan Stanley investment bank with the retail brokerage and credit card issuer Dean Witter Discover.

"There are now Dean Witter people up in the Morgan Stanley area so that guys running the deals can evaluate the potential for retail distribution at the same time they are looking at the institutional market," Scott said of the effect on underwriting.
Scott said there have already been some successful deals such as a preferred issue for Bank of New York Co Inc which demonstrated what Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter can do together.

Asked about the credit card business, which posted a three percent year-over-year profit gain reflecting a 49 percent increase in the provision for loan losses, Scott said the business in part is a function of consumer spending activity. "I think that we are confident that there is still potential for healthy margins and returns in the business."
He said there is a "very large untapped potential" for taking the credit card business beyond North America.
